<a id="主张-claim"></a>
## Claim

Along an actual finite trace under a fixed relational law, all existential endpoint possibilities are preserved exactly when a return path exists. Failure to return has a constructive lost endpoint witness; incomplete questions can hide this loss.

Canonical source: [BecomingReversibility.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/deeper/BecomingReversibility.lean)

<a id="沿革-history"></a>
## History

- 9 October 2026: checked structural connection and author counterreview registered. Helpers and repeated applications are not counted as independent foundational results.
- 14 October 2026, integration I3 (Ren: “a lot proofs are probably not integrated”): stated on the spine as an instance of core laws. With no premise the core (Becoming.Recurrence) proves, for every process, that every configuration reachable from s stays reachable from t exactly when t leads back to s (keeps_reach_iff_returns), that along a path from s to t the reachable configurations are the same exactly when the path can be undone (same_reach_iff_returns), and that no way back is a lost possibility with s itself as witness (not_returns_iff_loses). BecomingReversibility's reachability is the core's and a possibility is being at some reachable configuration (keeps_possible_iff_keeps_reach), so same_endpoint_possibilities_iff_return and irreversible_iff_endpoint_loss are these laws (same_endpoint_possibilities_iff_return_by_core, irreversible_iff_endpoint_loss_by_core), with empty axiom reports (scratch build; the receipt comes with the landing). The periphery proof and its receipt keep their scope; the bridge now imports BecomingReversibility, which the spine run compiles as an inherited module.
